Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard metadata variables such as `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `arch`, `url`, `depends`, and others, all using static or templated values derived from known constants or the declared `url`. The `source` arrays for each architecture reference release binaries from the project's official GitHub repository using predictable, versioned URLs. These are resolved at build time but are not downloaded during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. There is no command substitution, function execution, or external network interaction occurring in the global scope of the PKGBUILD. All variable assignments are declarative and do not involve execution of shell commands or external scripts. The `package()` function is defined but will not be executed during `--printsrcinfo`, so it is out of scope for this safety gate.

No obfuscated code, dynamic evaluation (`eval`), or data exfiltration attempts are present in the top-level context. The use of `::` in the source array is standard for renaming downloaded files and does not imply unsafe behavior. Checksums are provided and non-SKIPped, though even if they were skipped, that alone would not affect the safety of `--printsrcinfo`. Overall, sourcing this PKGBUILD for metadata extraction poses no risk of unintended code execution or data leakage.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No top-level malicious code; safe to parse.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- No top-level malicious code; safe to parse.

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The .SRCINFO file defines metadata for the `kandev-bin` package, a prebuilt binary distributed via the AUR. It specifies two sources — one for x86_64 and one for aarch64 — both pointing to release binaries hosted on the project's official GitHub repository (`https://github.com/kdlbs/kandev`). The URLs use HTTPS, and the SHA-256 checksums are explicitly provided and match standard practice for verifying binary integrity.

All dependencies and optional dependencies are standard system components (e.g., `git`, `docker`, `openssh`, `glibc`), consistent with the package's functionality as an AI coding agent orchestrator. The package provides `kandev` and conflicts with itself to prevent version clashes. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious scripts, or unauthorized network calls. The sources are pinned to specific release versions and archived binaries, not mutable references like git branches, ensuring reproducibility.

No dangerous build options or post-install hooks are present in this metadata file. The use of `!strip` and `!debug` is acceptable for a prebuilt binary package, as stripping debug symbols or enabling debug info is unnecessary when the binary is not compiled locally. Overall, the file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and shows no evidence of malicious intent.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR package metadata with verified binary sources</summary>
</security_assessment>

[1/2] Reviewing PKGBUILD...
+ Reviewed .SRCINFO. Status: SAFE -- Standard AUR package metadata with verified binary sources
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard AUR package for `kandev-bin`, a prebuilt CLI tool distributed from its official GitHub repository. The source URLs point directly to versioned release assets under the project's own repository (`https://github.com/kdlbs/kandev`), and checksums are provided for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures, ensuring integrity. The build process consists solely of extracting and installing prebuilt binaries into standard system paths, with no compilation or dynamic fetching at install time.

The package installs several binaries (including `kandev` and multiple `agentctl` variants) under `/usr/lib/kandev/bin`, and creates a symlink in `/usr/bin/kandev` for easy access. These operations are consistent with typical packaging practices for a multi-binary CLI tool. No network requests, dynamic code evaluation, or file manipulations outside the package directory occur in the `package()` function.

There are no signs of obfuscation, unauthorized data exfiltration, or execution of externally fetched code. The use of `!strip` and `!debug` is appropriate for a binary-only package. Optional dependencies are clearly declared and serve legitimate purposes (e.g., Docker for containerized agents, SSH for remote execution). All actions align with the declared purpose of the software.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard prebuilt binary package from official source with valid checksums.
</summary>
